name: Endowment supporting a Jerusalem hospital
description: In his account of his 1047 visit, Nasir-i Khusraw describes a Jerusalem hospital that gave many people medicine and medicinal drinks. Its physicians drew stipends from an endowment he calls a waqf.

impact.note: One traveller’s account of endowment-funded physician stipends at one hospital.

date.basis: Nasir-i Khusraw dates his arrival in Jerusalem to 5 Ramadan 438 AH, corresponding to 1047 in Le Strange’s translation. The hospital passage describes conditions during that visit.

events.statement: Nasir-i Khusraw reported that a Jerusalem hospital gave many people medicine and medicinal drinks and that its physicians received stipends from a waqf.
events.scope: The hospital’s reported operations in Fatimid-era Jerusalem during the 1047 visit.
events.caveats: The hospital’s founding date and the date of composition of the travel account are unknown. The account leaves open whether Nasir-i Khusraw inspected the hospital himself.

evidence.supports: Dates arrival to 5 Ramadan 438 AH and describes the Jerusalem hospital, its distribution of medicines and medicinal drinks, and physicians drawing stipends from a waqf.
Places Jerusalem under Fatimid rule, dates the visit to 1047 and translates the same account of an endowed hospital with remedies and paid physicians.
Dates the visit to 1047 and summarizes the stipend arrangement from Thackston’s English translation of the same account.

earliest_record.rationale: The 1047 visit is the earliest supported episode for the hospital’s endowment-funded physician stipends. The date of composition of the account is unknown.

caveats: The travel account names a waqf as the source of physician stipends. The patron, endowed assets, other expenses, patient eligibility, fees and founding date are unknown.

research.note: The Persian edition and the English renderings cited here transmit one medieval witness.

unresolved.note: Find an endowment deed, inscription or dated account identifying the donor, assets, founding date and operating terms. The travel text names the waqf as the source of stipends without identifying who endowed it.

evidence.supports: Names the waqf and describes its physician stipends.

unresolved.note: The adjoining reference to the Friday mosque and Wadi Jahannam leaves the hospital’s precise site open across editions. A contemporary description, deed or excavated inscription tying the hospital to a particular building would help test continuity with other Jerusalem institutions.

evidence.supports: The translation locates a wall of the Friday mosque by Wadi Jahannam and names Jerusalem as the location of the hospital.
